ex: Rousseau's 1762 book The Social Contract famously declares: “Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.”
Some argue that paying taxes is part of the social contract between citizens and their government.

why: Factual error: the book does not begin with that line; it comes after a foreword and an introductory passage, opening Book I, Chapter 1.

cloze.s: The faster a bowler rolls the ball, the more ___ it carries into the pins.

set.why: It explains why doubling a car's speed quadruples the energy that must be absorbed in a crash.

why: Cloze was physically wrong: a released bowling ball slows slightly down the lane, so its kinetic energy does not grow. 'Destructive power' in why was loose; four times the kinetic energy is the exact claim.

cloze.s: Robert Burns's line “O my Luve is like a red, red rose” is a famous ___.

why: Misquote: Burns's line is “O my Luve is like a red, red rose” (Poetry Foundation text), not “My love is like a red, red rose.”

cloze.s: Eye color is shaped by more than one ___, so predicting a baby's eye color from the parents' is not simple.

why: Faulty reasoning: siblings can differ in eye color even for single-gene traits, so 'which is why siblings can have different eye colors' does not follow from eye color being polygenic.

set.def: increase by a constant percentage each period, so the amount doubles at regular intervals and speeds up over time

why: 'Keeps doubling' was inaccurate; constant-percentage growth doubles at a fixed interval, not continuously.

ex: Ice floats on a lake because its density is lower than that of liquid water.
Olga pointed to the different density of oil and vinegar to explain why the oil floated on top of her salad dressing.

why: Density explains which liquid ends up on top, not why oil and vinegar separate (that is because they do not mix).

ex: Frederick Douglass recounted his years in slavery and his path to freedom in his autobiography.
Priya's grandmother is writing an autobiography for her grandchildren.

why: Risky claim: Douglass's best-known autobiography (the 1845 Narrative) deliberately left out how he escaped; the details came only in a later book (1881). Reworded so it is true of all his autobiographies.

set.note: Named after Massachusetts governor Elbridge Gerry, who in 1812 signed a redistricting bill creating a district whose odd shape was mocked as a salamander.

why: Precision: the legislature drew the map; Gerry signed the bill. 'Whose 1812 district map' overstated his role.

set.why: It protects online banking, shopping, messaging and the data stored on phones and laptops.

why: Stored passwords are normally protected by hashing, not encryption, so naming them was technically wrong.

set.why: Examples like the Epic of Gilgamesh, Homer's Iliad, and India's Mahabharata are foundational works of world literature.

why: Overstatement: the Mahabharata (composed roughly 400 BCE to 400 CE) is not among the oldest surviving works of literature.

ex: Ancient Athens is often called the birthplace of democracy, though only adult male citizens could vote.
Kwame's civics teacher explained that democracy depends on fair elections and an informed public.

why: Inaccurate: free men who were not citizens, such as resident foreigners (metics), could not vote in Athens.

ex: Sofia opened her web browser and typed in the airline's address to check her flight.
If a page will not load properly, try clearing your web browser's cache and cookies.

why: The standard troubleshooting step is clearing the cache and cookies; clearing history does not fix loading problems.

ex: MRSA is a type of staph bacteria known for its antibiotic resistance.
Farmers were urged to limit drug use in livestock to slow antibiotic resistance.

why: MRSA is a strain of bacteria (methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus), not an infection; matches the CDC wording.

set.def: a low, often fan-shaped area of land formed where a river deposits sediment as it enters a sea or lake

why: Not all deltas are fan-shaped; the Mississippi delta in the cloze is a bird's-foot delta.

set.def: a cold, treeless region of low plants and short summers, often with permanently frozen subsoil, found in the Arctic and high mountains

why: Alpine (mountain) tundra usually has no permafrost, so frozen subsoil cannot be part of the definition for both kinds.

ex: To fence the garden, Kwame added its sides, 12 meters plus 8 meters, and doubled them for a perimeter of 40 meters.
Security guards patrolled the perimeter of the stadium before the game.

why: Unit missing from the answer (40 meters).

ex: Tucson's desert climate means hot summers and very little rain.
Olga moved from Phoenix to Seattle and had to adjust to a much rainier climate.

why: Overgeneralization: much of Arizona (e.g. Flagstaff, at high elevation) does not have a desert climate.

set.why: Web email, photo backups, streaming services and much business software run this way.

why: 'Most business software now' is a time-sensitive, unverified figure; softened to a stable claim.

cloze.s: In the ___ 3/8, the bottom number shows that the whole pizza was cut into eight equal slices.

why: Old cloze ('you have eaten the ___ 3/8 of it') was ungrammatical. Ratio removed because 3/8 can also be read as a ratio.
3/8 can also be read as a ratio, so ratio could fill the new cloze.
High cholesterol is also symptomless until damage is done (and is sometimes also called a silent killer), so it fits the cloze.
'The computer worked fine, but the web browser kept crashing whenever Maria opened a large file' makes sense, so the browser also fits the cloze.

Its definition is too close to separation of powers (keeping any branch from becoming too powerful); learners could defensibly pick either.
'A loan with a 5 percent annual compound interest costs less than one at 9 percent' also makes sense.

'The passing ratio was 75%' could be defended in the cloze.
